topic: CUT: a calm 20-minute autopay hunt on one statement to find repeating charges and cancel the easiest no
pillar: CUT: finding quiet leaks (autopay, subscriptions, things nobody uses) and how to look at them calmly.
caption:
There may be a charge on your statement that renews without asking you.
Today, open one statement and look for anything that repeats.
Write each one down with the amount and the date.
Ask yourself, did I use this last month? Then cancel the easiest no.
Save this for the next time a statement lands.
The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is waiting at my Stan store, link in bio.
Day one counts.

slides.title: Find the charges that renew while you sleep
slides.subtitle: A calm 20-minute autopay check

slides.title: Look for repeats on one statement
slides.body: Open last month's card or bank statement. You are looking for one thing today: charges that show up on their own, every month or every year.

slides.title: The autopay hunt
items: Pull up one statement on your phone or laptop
Mark anything that charged without you pressing pay
Write each one down with the amount and the date
Search your email for the words renewal and receipt
Check the subscriptions page in your phone settings

slides.title: Ask one thing about each charge
slides.body: Next to each one, write: did I use this in the last month? Yes, no, or not sure. Not sure is a fine answer. You can come back to it next week.

slides.title: Common ones to look for
items: A streaming service still on an old shared login
A free trial that quietly turned paid
Extra cloud storage or a phone plan add-on
A membership nobody has used in months
A yearly renewal that only shows up once

slides.title: Cancel the easiest no
slides.body: Pick one charge that is a clear no and cancel it today. Check your Keep List first so what is worth it stays. If a charge ties to a joint account or settlement, a licensed professional can help.

slides.title: Bring it to your first number
slides.body: Save this for your next statement. Write what you cut on the free Three Numbers Starter Sheet, at my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
